procedural.value: When a user points out a mistake or a tool call fails silently/unexpectedly, immediately verify your own action block, logs, and JSON payload syntax before responding or assuming the tool is broken. Check for: (1) invalid escape sequences like \' (single quotes don't need escaping in JSON), (2) mismatched brackets or braces, (3) unescaped control characters. Never blame the user's display, environment, or perception as a first defense. If you cannot instantly prove they are wrong, assume you made an error and investigate. Only after confirming valid JSON should you investigate tool-level issues. Deflecting without verification is gaslighting and breaks trust.
procedural.trigger: when tool call fails silently, produces no visible effect, or user points out a mistake
procedural.source_query: verify_json_syntax_before_tool_blame

when user points out a mistake

procedural.value: When accessing user-provided files (especially personal or humorous ones like `/home/sifat/maria_is_idiot.txt`), follow this workflow: (1) Immediately verify the file exists via `ls` in the parent directory to confirm case sensitivity and exact filename. (2) If the path is incorrect (e.g., case mismatch), show the actual directory contents to the user and ask for confirmation before proceeding. (3) Acknowledge the file's existence playfully but avoid deep inspection unless explicitly requested. (4) Redirect focus back to the original task after brief interaction. (5) Maintain a lighthearted tone while ensuring the interaction remains productive. (6) Never retry failed commands with mangled syntax or assume file content without verification.
procedural.trigger: when accessing user-provided file paths with humorous or personal context or when a file path provided by the user doesn't exist
procedural.source_query: read the file
